crm_notes:
Summary and call notes (shorthand):
- Customer: Miralux Product Labs (mid-market SaaS; product analytics). Building in-app assistant and internal doc search.
- Trial use: Hosted API used for 8 weeks across support-agent chat and document search indexing. Team: 6 engineers + PMs.
- Traffic observed during hosted trial: typical steady-state QPS 8-15. Synthetic peak tests: 40-50 QPS sustained for 10m.
- Concurrency expectations for production Dedicated: 40-100 concurrent generation sessions depending on feature flags and holiday spikes. Primary SLA target: p95 latency <200ms for short-turn dialog (<=64 tokens).
- Token mix (measured during trial): ~72% short-turn chat messages (~25-60 tokens), ~18% mid-length summarizations (~200-800 tokens), ~10% long-form generation/analytics (~1k-2k tokens). Average token per request ~240 (skewed by occasional long jobs).
- Cost sensitivity: product team wants predictable unit cost; finance wants 6-12 month committed pricing with clear overage behavior. Estimated target ARR for Dedicated: $75k-140k/year depending on discounts and min commit.
- Model preferences: prefer open LLaMA-derived variants for cost but willing to use Redwood-verified variants; need quantization guidance for 8-bit/4-bit trade-offs.
- Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to a lower-capacity variant in other region if Dedicated pool saturated; also want model-pin for regulatory reasons.
- Security/compliance asks: SSO/SAML integration, audit logging retention (1 year), KMS for key management, data residency clarification (US region only), purge/retention controls for support transcripts.
- POC deliverables requested: 1) Dedicated capacity sizing worksheet with QPS -> GPU mapping, concurrency vs batch size recommendations, expected token-hour estimates; 2) Pricing scenarios (monthly commit tiers + overage); 3) Security evidence (SOC2 + KMS integration guide) and security questionnaire answers.
- Quotes from meetings: "We need predictability — spikes kill our margins; batching is great but we can't sacrifice p95 latency for short interactions." - Head of Product (A. Lopez).
- Notes on infra: they run on AWS primarily (us-east-1), require VPC peering option for Dedicated and prefer encryption keys in their AWS KMS.
- Next steps: SE (Priya) to deliver Dedicated sizing workbook v1 by 2026-02-18. AE (Jordan) to coordinate executive pricing call w/ Miralux CFO for week of 2026-02-22. Security team to respond to questionnaire by 2026-02-20.
- Risks: If security responses delayed, procurement committee will push timeline into Q3. If synthetic peak >60 QPS, they may push for reserved burst capacity which increases cost.
